pr_title: Fix event expiration to prevent losing events
pr_body: Fixes https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/8524 by ensuring the last events are never expired from a table. Without this change, new event IDs could be unintentionally generated starting from 1, while optimizations tell the generate function to look at a higher ID. All of those newer events would then never be logged.
pr_comments: @zwass What was the conclusion here? I know you talked for awhile at Office Hours about this. Is it ready for merge?
I believe it's ready but I am hoping that @alessandrogario will review it because it's deep in the events code.

issue_context.title: Osquery loses events due to optimization errors under specific conditions
comments:
I have multiple ideas for possible fixes, and I think the related code should be scrutinized for similar issues.

1) Leave at least one event when expiring events so that the future calculation always generates a monotonically increasing ID.
2) When using the `optimize_eid`, also check the `optimize_time` to ensure we aren't optimizing away events that are from a later time than the last query that generated results.

cc @alessandrogario I think you wrote a lot of this code and I would love your input.

> Leave at least one event when expiring events so that the future calculation always generates a monotonically increasing ID.

I think some folks use the optimization/expiration as a simple way to create deliver-once semantics. Stashing the ID might work?

review_comments: I don't really understand how optimize prevents it from being returned. Or how this tests it.

Optimization keeps track of the highest eventid and then when the generate function is called any event with a lower ID is skipped when returning rows. The test for optimization verifies that behavior.
